1.explanation: All of the listed functions participate in the discovery, bundling, serving and execution of rendering test cases in the rendering/ folder. webpack.config.js’s caseDirs filter and entry object determine which test cases are built. The serve, renderEach, render, getOutdated and main functions in rendering/test.js handle spinning up the server, iterating over each case, comparing screenshots and skipping up-to-date tests. To unify both test suites, these pieces of logic must be extended or refactored to include the test/rendering folder’s cases and apply a single entry/build/run mechanism for all rendering tests.
1.bug_scenario: The project currently maintains two separate rendering test suites: one under the rendering/ directory (with its own webpack.config.js and test runner in rendering/test.js) and another set of tests under test/rendering. Both use different mechanisms to discover, build, serve and compare screenshots. The goal is to unify them into a single consistent testing pipeline.

2.explanation: All of these functions in rendering/test.js implement the core rendering test workflow: discovering cases (getHref), serving files (serve, indexHandler, notFound), driving Puppeteer (exposeRender, renderPage), capturing and diffing screenshots (parsePNG, match, getScreenshotsMismatch), iterating through cases and managing pass files (renderEach, render), filtering based on modification times (getOutdated), and the overall orchestration (main). To unify rendering tests, this harness must be merged with (or replaced by) the tests under test/rendering so that there is only one code path for executing and validating rendering output.
2.bug_scenario: The project currently has two separate mechanisms for running rendering tests: one based on the “rendering/cases” directory with its own Webpack entrypoints and a Puppeteer-driven harness (rendering/test.js), and another set of tests living under test/rendering. This split leads to duplicated test logic (case discovery, server setup, screenshot capture and diffing, pass file management, etc.). The goal is to unify both approaches into a single, consistent rendering test framework.
